title: The AR in Star
kidRule: A and R usually team up to say 'ar', which sounds just like the name of the letter R! (After a W the sound changes, like in WARM.)
hint: Listen for the 'ar' sound, the one a pirate loves to say. It takes two letters to spell it. Which two?
reminder: The 'ar' sound is spelled A-R: the A comes first, then the R.

check.question: Why does SPARKLE have an A before the R?
check.correctAnswer: Because A and R team up to make the 'ar' sound!
distractors: Because the letter R can never follow a P
Because every long word needs the letter A

words.def: To shine with lots of tiny flashes of light.
words.sent: The snow began to sparkle in the morning sun.
words.story: Diamonds sparkle because light bends and bounces around inside them before it shines back out!
words.card: One tiny *spark* made the whole unicorn *sparkle*!

words.def: A home that is one set of rooms inside a bigger building.
words.sent: Our apartment is on the fifth floor.
words.story: People in ancient Rome lived in apartment buildings too, and some of them were five or more floors tall!
words.card: The best *part* of our *apartment* is the giraffe who lives upstairs!

words.def: A loud sound that warns you or wakes you up.
words.sent: The alarm rang at seven in the morning.
words.story: Meerkats take turns standing guard. When the lookout spots danger, it barks an alarm call and everyone dives underground!
words.card: The octopus used one *arm* to switch off the *alarm* and seven to keep snoozing!

words.def: Someone you work, play, or dance with as a team.
words.sent: Pick a partner for the three-legged race.
words.story: A clownfish and a sea anemone make a great team. The anemone's stinging arms keep the fish safe, and the fish helps keep its partner clean!
words.card: My *art* *partner* is a snail, so our painting takes all week!

words.def: A person who builds and fixes things made of wood.
words.sent: The carpenter built a treehouse with a tiny door.
words.story: Carpenter ants do not eat wood. They chew tunnels through it to build their nests!
words.card: The *carpenter* built a wooden car with a *pen* for a steering wheel!

words.def: A knitted sweater that opens down the front, usually with buttons.
words.sent: Grandma knitted me a red cardigan for winter.
words.story: The cardigan is named after the Earl of Cardigan, a British army leader whose soldiers wore knitted jackets about 170 years ago!
words.card: I keep a birthday *card* in the pocket of my *cardigan*, just in case!

words.def: Something you aim at and try to hit.
words.sent: Her arrow hit the middle of the target.
words.story: In the Olympic Games, archers shoot at a target that is 70 meters away. That is longer than half a soccer field!
words.card: The clumsy wizard could not *get* one marshmallow near the *target*!

words.def: The time when farmers pick the crops that are ready.
words.sent: Everyone helped with the apple harvest in the fall.
words.story: The full moon closest to the start of fall is called the Harvest Moon, because its bright light helped farmers keep working after sunset!
words.card: The scarecrow wore his fanciest *vest* for the pumpkin *harvest*!

words.def: A talk where people disagree and each one tries to show they are right.
words.sent: The twins had an argument about whose turn it was.
words.story: The word argue ends with an E, but that E disappears in this longer word, which makes it one of the most often misspelled words in English!
words.card: The *argument* ended when we both got bubble *gum* stuck in our hair!

words.def: A small animal covered in bony armor that digs burrows in the ground.
words.sent: An armadillo scurried across the dusty road.
words.story: The three-banded armadillo can roll itself into a tight ball, like a little armored soccer ball, to stay safe!
words.card: The *armadillo* curled up inside a *dill* pickle jar for a nap!
